Navigation

Getting between places. Top-level destinations belong in a drawer, a rail or a bottom bar; views within one destination belong in tabs; actions on the current view belong in a menu.

App bars

The bar at the top of a screen: where you are, how to get out, and the actions that apply to the whole view. It is the same color as the page, not an accent band and not a raised surface, so the chrome reads as the edge of the window rather than as a strip laid across it. Nothing separates it from the content until there is content passing underneath, and then a soft falloff appears beneath it — the bar at the top of this page does it as you scroll. These stages are the page color so the bars sit flush with it, as they really do.

Drawers

A modal drawer slides over the content and dims it; a docked drawer stays put on wide screens. Escape and a click on the scrim both close the modal form.

Content area

The docked drawer is part of the layout rather than an overlay, so nothing is dimmed and no scrim is needed. Below the large breakpoint it is usually swapped for the modal form.

Navigation rail

Three to seven destinations on a medium screen, in less width than a drawer and with more room than a bottom bar.

inbox Inbox star_border Starred send Sent delete Bin

Inbox

The active destination is marked with both color and a pill behind its glyph, so it does not rely on color alone.

Bottom navigation

Three to five top-level destinations within thumb reach on a phone.

home Home search Explore notifications7 Alerts person Profile

Tabs

Peer views of the same thing. Arrow keys move between tabs and the underline follows the selection.

Overview

The first panel is visible by default. Panels are plain containers — the script only toggles the hidden attribute.

Activity

Each panel is referenced from its tab with aria-controls.

Settings

Only the selected tab is in the tab order; the rest are reached with the arrow keys.

Billing

The indicator is measured from the active tab, so it works with labels of any width.

With icons, filling the width

Menus

Actions anchored to the control that opened them. Only one is open at a time; Escape or a click anywhere else dismisses it.

PatternDestinationsBest at
